name: Abimelech
role: Son of Gideon who made himself king at Shechem
summary: Gideon's son by a concubine from Shechem. Backed by his mother's kin, he hired men with silver from the temple of Baal-berith, killed his seventy brothers on one stone, and was made king at Shechem. Only Jotham escaped, and told the fable of the trees choosing the bramble for king. Three years later Shechem turned against him; he destroyed it, and at Thebez a woman dropped a millstone on his head.
body: Gideon had refused to be king; his son asks the Shechemites whether it is better for seventy men to rule them or one who is their own flesh and bone. From Mount Gerizim, Jotham tells how the olive, the fig and the vine declined to reign, and the bramble offered its shade, or else fire.

God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem. He razes the city and sows it with salt, and burns a thousand people in the stronghold of the tower. At Thebez, as he approaches the tower door to burn it, a woman throws down an upper millstone; he tells his armour-bearer to kill him, so that no one will say a woman did. Judges says God repaid the wickedness he had done to his father.

media.caption: The death of Abimelech (Judges 9:53–54), Gustave Doré, 1866.
